prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1055; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Received first notice of loss from the claimant, who reports being struck while turning left at an intersection. The claimant is not represented by an attorney and describes neck and back strain following the impact.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of the incident. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the scene. Responding officers and a witness statement are consistent with the claimant's location.

Entry 4: Claimant gave a recorded statement describing the sequence of events. The account matched the one given during first notice and was consistent in every conversation so far.

Entry 5: Photos from the scene confirm the general point of impact and the vehicle positions. No independent witnesses have come forward beyond those listed in the police report.

Entry 6: Inspected the vehicle. A few old scratches are visible on the rear panel that may predate this collision, and I have noted them separately for the appraiser.

Entry 7: Medical records show the reported neck and back strain. The kind and force of the impact appear well matched to these injuries.

Entry 8: Reviewed the treatment history. Care followed a typical course and tapered as the claimant's condition improved. No prior injury to the same body areas is known from the records obtained.

Entry 9: Appraiser notes it is not yet clear whether all of the listed damage resulted from this impact. The estimate is on hold pending a closer look at the older marks.

Entry 10: Spoke again with the claimant, who repeated the same account of the turning collision without changes. No new information was offered that alters the file.

Entry 11: Current status: liability and coverage are being reviewed together with medical treatment progress. Next step is to finalize the damage split once the appraiser's supplemental report is received.
